name: Meso-zeaxanthin
short: Only with lutein and zeaxanthin: 6-month blood tests in range in 44 healthy people (cholesterol and LDL out of range from the start); no serious adverse events in 62 with glaucoma. Rats: no toxicity.
text: Human safety data come only from small trials of meso-zeaxanthin combined with lutein and zeaxanthin. In a 6-month placebo-controlled trial in 44 healthy people, clinical pathology tests stayed within the normal reference range (apart from cholesterol and LDL values that were already outside it before supplementation), and the authors found no adverse clinical implications. In an 18-month placebo-controlled trial in 62 people with open-angle glaucoma, no serious adverse events were noted; the abstract does not report milder adverse events. In a 13-week study in rats given meso-zeaxanthin by mouth, no compound-related clinical, biochemical or pathological changes were seen at up to 200 mg/kg/day, and it did not cause mutations in bacterial laboratory tests; these are animal and laboratory findings. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
